name: Precision oncology and liquid biopsies
summary: Molecular tests help select cancer treatments and detect tumour signals from blood, sometimes reducing the need for invasive sampling.
useCase: An oncologist uses a tumour DNA result to select a targeted treatment or monitor possible recurrence, with confirmatory clinical assessment.
whyNow: Clinical testing volumes are expanding and blood-based screening has reached specific regulatory approvals. Different applications have very different evidence: therapy selection, residual disease and screening must not be treated as interchangeable.

mainstream.scope: Routine molecular profiling and evidence-backed blood testing in selected oncology pathways; not universal multi-cancer population screening.
mainstream.rationale: Existing test volume and growing treatment matching support routine oncology use this decade. Screening benefit requires outcome evidence, reimbursement and appropriate follow-up; those applications can take longer.

metric.name: Guardant oncology clinical tests
metric.scope: Guardant clinical oncology volume; excludes screening and biopharma tests
metric.limitations: One company’s clinical oncology volume, including products beyond liquid biopsy; not the total sector or unique patients. Annual endpoints are comparable within the disclosed company series. No invented 2026 full-year total.
metric.futureNote: No defensible like-for-like external forecast is available for this KPI. The forward maturity path is a separately labelled analyst scenario, not a numerical adoption forecast.

milestones.text: Clinical test volume reached 124,800 at the same operator.
No comparable 2023 numerical observation is included in this chart.
Guardant reported 206,700 oncology clinical tests for the year.
The same volume series reached approximately 276,000 tests.
The February 2026 results establish the latest full-year observation; Freenome completed its public listing in July.

tailwinds: More therapies require molecular patient selection
Blood sampling can support repeat monitoring
Sequencing and analytical pipelines offer supplier exposure
bottlenecks: Low tumour shedding can cause false negatives
Early detection is useful only with beneficial follow-up
Coverage decisions differ by cancer type, indication and payer
watchMetrics: Reimbursed tests and repeat ordering by indication
Sensitivity at early stages plus false-positive workup burden
Prospective evidence that test-guided care improves outcomes
